title: incident-bot: on-call autodiagnostics telemetry and sampling improvements
author: Maya Chen
description: Context and motivation: On-call autodiagnostics (incident-bot + slo-toolkit helpers) have been producing useful suggestions, but we lack stable telemetry to measure signal quality and sampling behavior in production. This PR adds lightweight telemetry hooks and a deterministic sampling control to help SRE and product measure: 1) autodiagnostics invocation rate, 2) suggestion acceptance/feedback rate, 3) runbook link click-through, and 4) per-slo sampling coverage. Goals: (a) make it easy to track quality/regressions when changing heuristics, (b) reduce cardinality and PII risk for metrics, (c) configurable sampling for heavy customers to control cost. What changed: - incident-bot: add telemetry hooks around diagnostics generation, runbook scoring, and suggestion rendering. Metrics use low-cardinality tags (service, env, heuristic_version) and hashed identifiers for bucketed sampling. - slo-toolkit: introduce new utilities for deterministic sampling (seeded hashing) and exposure API so other components can adopt same sampling logic. - runbooks: add optional runbook metadata used by incident-bot to rank quicklinks and emit structured tags for observability. - docs: update on-call runbook and telemetry runbook with examples and recommended dashboards. - tests: unit tests for sampling utilities and telemetry emission; small e2e simulated run to validate metric shapes. Implementation notes: - Telemetry emits counters and histograms to our observability client; high-cardinality fields were explicitly removed and hashed into low-cardinality buckets. - Sampling uses FNV-1a hashed concat(service + user_bucket) mod 10000 to derive deterministic percent sampling; default sampling configured to 5% with override via feature flag. - Backwards compatibility: all new metrics are additive and optional; no changes to public API surface. Checklist: - [x] Add telemetry hooks and sampling util - [x] Ensure metric tags limited to low cardinality - [x] Add unit tests for sampling - [x] Update runbook and docs - [x] Add feature flag and config for sampling rate How tested: - Unit tests added and passing locally and in CI. - Local integration run simulating 10k incidents with deterministic sampling validated expected sampling ratio within 0.2% of configured rate. - Canary rollout plan: enable on 10% of workers for 24h, verify metric shapes and absence of PII, then roll to 100% if stable. Rollout/Rollback: feature gated behind release flag incident_bot.autodiag.telemetry.enabled; rollback by disabling flag. Related: ENG-9123 (autodiag telemetry), SUP-3472 (customer reported excessive suggestions), ENG-9180 (sampling utility extraction).
commits: 4 commits: 1) add sampling util and unit tests; 2) telemetry hooks in incident-bot diagnostics flow; 3) runbook metadata and docs updates; 4) fix unit tests and CI flakes
review_comments: Ethan: Asked to reduce cardinality of metrics and avoid user IDs in tags; requested proof of no PII leakage in tests. Radhika: Requested configurable default sampling to 5% and added suggestion to surface the heuristic_version tag. Lars: Suggested deterministic sampling util be shared in slo-toolkit and added a small API change to allow seed override for deterministic replay. Diego: flagged a flaky test in CI (tests/diagnostics/test_autodiag_telemetry.py) which failed intermittently due to timing; author updated tests to be time-independent. Author responses: updated metrics to hashed buckets, added unit that asserts no raw user identifiers emitted, extracted sampling util to slo-toolkit, added feature flag and env var for sampling rate, and fixed the flaky timing assertion. Final approvals from Ethan and Radhika after fixes. CI: initial run had 1 flaky test failure; reran and all checks passed.
release_notes:
- incident-bot: emit low-cardinality telemetry for autodiagnostics (invocations, suggestion_acceptance, runbook_clicks)
- slo-toolkit: deterministic sampling utility for consistent percent-based sampling across services
- Docs: examples and recommended dashboards for autodiag metrics
- Feature flag: incident_bot.autodiag.telemetry.enabled (default: off), sampling default 5%
notes_for_ops: Feature gated behind incident_bot.autodiag.telemetry.enabled; default sampling 5% controlled via INCIDENT_AUTODIAG_SAMPLING_PCT env var. Watch for metric cardinality; ensure hashed buckets are used when querying. Canary to 10% workers for 24h before full rollout.
testing_summary: Unit tests added for sampling util and telemetry emission. Local integration sim validated sampling ratio on 10k simulated events. CI passed after rerun (one flaky test fixed).
risk_assessment: Low: additive metrics only, feature flagged. Risk of increased observability cost mitigated by default 5% sampling and low-cardinality tagging. No PII expected to be emitted; unit tests assert that.
follow_up_tasks: 1) Create Grafana dashboard panels for new metrics and add to on-call runbook (ENG-9240). 2) Monitor suggestion_acceptance rate for 7 days after full rollout and tune sampling or heuristics. 3) Consider exposing sampling util in other services that call autodiag.
changelog_entry: incident-bot: add autodiagnostics telemetry + deterministic sampling (feature-flagged)
